summary: Tested Diwali/Regular order types end-to-end. Backend: 10/10 new pytest cases pass (deadline open/closed/today boundary, diwali 400 when closed, regular/default 503 payment, invalid order_type 422, bad deadline format 422, settings auth 401, admin orders return order_type without _id). Old regression suite 26/26 pass. Frontend: banner countdown to 8 Nov plus note 'Last date for Diwali orders: 5 November'. Checkout picker has Diwali selected by default and sends order_type 'diwali', which gives a 503 toast. With the deadline set to 2026-10-01 from the admin Delivery tab, the banner shows 'Diwali orders closed — regular orders welcome', the Diwali button is disabled, Regular is selected, and the POST sends 'regular'. Admin Orders tags show Diwali/Regular and the filter counts All(2)/Diwali(1)/Regular(1) filter correctly. The settings save keeps rates and rounding (1.25kg abroad round_up = ₹1400). The mobile 390px banner wraps cleanly with no horizontal overflow.
critical_code_review_comments: Order-type buttons lack aria-pressed/role=radio for accessibility (minor).
diwali_open uses string comparison of ISO dates in IST, which is correct, and the deadline day itself counts as open (verified).
CheckoutDialog initial orderType state depends on settings at mount; it is guarded by `type = diwaliOpen ? orderType : 'regular'`, so it is safe.
